title: Postmortem: campaign-triggered token-bucket refill skew led to staggered regional throttling and SLO drift
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: During a high-traffic marketing event on 2025-02-18 we observed progressive regional request throttling that caused p95/p99 SLO erosion for text-generation routes over a 3 hour window. This ticket captures timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and follow-up action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-18 09:12 UTC — SLO alert triggered: generation.p99_latency > 800ms in eu-west-1 and us-west-2
2025-02-18 09:18 UTC — Console shows sustained 15% 429 rate on generation API in eu-west-1; traffic surge from campaign confirmed by Growth
2025-02-18 09:33 UTC — Oncall increased token-bucket refill for eu-west-1 by 2x (manual override); partial recovery observed in eu-west-1
2025-02-18 09:50 UTC — us-east-1 and ap-southeast-1 begin showing elevated 5xx ratios due to cascading retries and heavier fanout; regional circuit breakers (CB) began opening asymmetrically
2025-02-18 10:05 UTC — Emergency rollback of recent CB cooldown tuning (PR #14522) to previous parameters; global rate limiter set to permissive for 20 minutes
2025-02-18 11:30 UTC — Traffic normalizes; SLOs return within targets after full rollback and token refill normalization
2025-02-20 — Deeper analysis begins: control plane config computation and canary telemetry review
2025-02-25 — Code fix PR #14610 merged to correct integer truncation in region-refill calculation and to add test coverage
2025-03-03 — New canary release with stricter rollout checks and automated region-simulated load tests deployed to staging
impact_summary: Customer-facing generation endpoints experienced elevated 429/5xx and tail latency during a peak marketing surge for ~3 hours. Overall incidence led to a 0.6% p99 availability degradation for affected routes in eu-west-1 and secondary impact in neighboring regions via retries and fanout amplification. No customer data was exposed. Several paying customers reported increased error rates and filed tickets.
root_cause: A recent change to the control-plane token-bucket refill math (introduced in PR #14522) used an integer division path for per-region refill rates under high scale, causing non-primary regions to calculate refill_rate ~= floor(refill_nominal * region_weight / 100). For small region weights this resulted in zero refill increments for short intervals. Simultaneously, a CB cooldown tuning increased the window before a circuit attempts soft-recovery, causing staggered, asymmetric healing across regions. The combination produced progressive regional throttling that amplified via client retries and cross-region fanout.
detection_and_response: SLO alerts and per-route 429 dashboards triggered the incident detection
Oncall ran the troubleshooting playbook (runbook v2.1) and escalated to runtime-leads
First mitigation was a manual token refill override per-region via admin API
Rollback of the recent CB cooldown change restored symmetric healing behavior
Post-incident, monitoring panels were extended with a dedicated 'refill_rate' timeseries per-region and synthetic probes added to surface zero-increment anomalies
mitigation: Immediate: manual increase of token-bucket refill for impacted regions and permissive global rate limit for 20 minutes
Immediate: rolled back CB cooldown change (PR #14522 revert) to previous stable parameters
Short-term: hotfix to control plane that converts refill math to fixed-point arithmetic and adds a minimum refill floor (merged PR #14610)
Medium-term: add pre-deploy canary tests that simulate small-region loads and verify refill > 0 under all region_weight combinations
Long-term: improve circuit-breaker soft-recovery heuristics to prevent long asymmetric healing windows and add a rollback safety to CB parameter flips
